title: Monza local Roman ceremonial order: H14, with sacramentary and reception gaps

traditions.label: Monza local Roman ceremonial order
traditions.scope: The local annual order of San Giovanni Battista in Monza attested by H14, distinguished from Monza-held sacramentaries and Ambrosian books.
traditions.coverage_note: One bounded order-book state; no complete Mass text, continuous sequence, or whole-book recension is reconstructed.

sources.title: Frisi, Memorie storiche di Monza III (1794), local order excerpt
sources.inspection: Whole University of Illinois digitization acquired, 394 PDF pages. Printed pp. 190–191, 195 (PDF pp. 220–221, 225) visually inspected; other Monza catalogue passages read in extracted text. Entry CLXXXVII describes and partially edits the local order, historically Milan Cathedral B.43; printed pp. 79–82 describe F.1/101 under former E.III / CXXVI. This is an eighteenth-century witness to the manuscript and a partial edition, not original manuscript-image collation. Frisi III, p. 190, note 18, reports that the words identifying Ecclesia Modoetiensis were erased but still legible in vestiges; modern H14 identity and local-order classification are independently supported by the 2018 census and the critical-edition review.
sources.limitations: Partial printed edition with eighteenth-century editorial observations; no original H14 image collation. The earlier Pontificale entry CLXXXVI on the left of p. 190 must not be merged into the local order beginning on the right.

sources.title: Baroffio, Sodi and Suski, Italian libri ordinari census (2018), p. 73
sources.inspection: Whole Latinitas series nova VI (2018), vol.1 acquired, 160 PDF pages. Baroffio, Sodi and Suski, I libri ordinari di origine italiana: guida ai manoscritti pretridentini, p. 73 (PDF p. 73), Monza entry visually inspected: H-14 ff. 47–74, Ordinarium, XII–XIII centuries, Monza; cites Dell’Oro–Mambretti (2001). Nearby B-14/121 is explicitly an Ambrosian Manuale fragment, not H14.
sources.limitations: Century range is palaeographic attestation, not first use, effectiveness, or a continuous lifespan.

sources.title: Pietro Messa, review of Liber ordinarius Modoetiensis (2003)
sources.inspection: Complete university HTML review by Pietro Messa, Antonianum 78/1 (2003), pp. 187–190 acquired and read. It separates H14 calendar-obituary ff. 1–46 from local order ff. 47–74; identifies edition A pp. 53–77 parallel Mass/Office books, pp. 251–276 initiation, pp. 375–382 Roman rite according to Monza custom, and critical text pp. 431–541. Review evidence is not direct inspection of the 2001 edition.
sources.limitations: The 2001 critical text and apparatus are not directly acquired or collated; conclusions are attributed to that edition through this review.

stages.label: Monza H14 local Roman ceremonial order
stages.scope: Annual local ceremonial order in H14 ff. 47–74; printed excerpts and modern manuscript identity, not a complete altar Mass book.
stages.witness_label: Monza Biblioteca Capitolare H14 ff. 47–74, Liber ordinarius Modoetiensis
stages.summary: A shelfmarked local order coordinates Monza's annual worship; original printed excerpts preserve Christmas and Easter Mass/Communion and processional directions. The critical edition describes Roman liturgy according to Monza custom.

evidence.claim: Identifies the manuscript constituent, Monza origin and XII–XIII palaeographic dating.

Frisi prints the local-church attribution from still-legible vestiges of erased wording (p. 190, note 18); his excerpts give Christmas Mass and Communion and Easter baptismal, Mass and processional directions. Modern H14 identification is independently supported by the census and edition review.

evidence.locus: Review of edition A chapters 4, 6, 9 and critical text: pp. 53–77, 251–276, 375–382, 431–541
evidence.claim: Distinguishes calendar-obituary from order; attributes Roman rite according to Monza custom to the edition, with specific Ambrosian initiation parallels.

stages.limitations: No complete H14 text, original manuscript collation, exact copying year, promulgation act or revision is established. Liber ordinarius is an order book; its title does not identify a Mass Ordinary. Frisi associated copying with a 1256 bequest; that older report is not used to narrow the modern broad century range.
stages.reception: The local order prescribes ceremonial practice for Monza. Frisi's local title attribution rests on still-legible erased wording; the census and edition review separately support H14 identity and classification. No first celebration, uniform observance or continuity through 1578 is established.

gaps.missing: Direct H14 original leaves and the 2001 critical text, its pericope and Mass-book references, apparatus and layers; exact continuity or changes are not collated.
gaps.next_source: H14 ff. 47r–74v complete images, compared with Dell’Oro–Mambretti (2001), volume A pp. 431–541; consult chapters pp. 53–77, 251–276, 375–382 and indices 545–594 for exact component crosswalks. Frisi (1794), vol. III pp. 190–201 is only a partial earlier edition.
gaps.consequence: No complete altar book, anaphora, revision, textual ancestry, or first-use date is asserted.

gaps.missing: F.1/101 constituent dates, foliation, exact Canon and mixed ritual layers; Berengar 98/89 identity/date/origin conflict and cathedral reception; relation to H14.
gaps.next_source: F.1/101 full images plus Dold–Gamber (1957) and Chavasse (1985) pp. 3–29; treasury 98/89 full images ff. 1v–5v, 46v–49r, 115v–125v; compare Belloni–Ferrari pp. 194–196, Hoffmann (2005) p. 71 and Westwell (2024) pp. 419–425. For damaged Berengar text obtain Vallicelliana T58 and Ambrosiana Fondo Varisco N.I.6inf inserto 43 copies. Lead (2026-10-22): Delmoro, ACME 2/2014, p. 73, prints Baldassarre Cipolla's 1595–96 visitation inventory of the cathedral treasury, which lists a Missale Sancti Gregorii with gilt boards and a Libellus Sancti Gregorii written in gold letters; nothing identifies either with Berengar 98/89, F.1/101 or another surviving codex.
gaps.consequence: Catalogue holdings, royal chapel use and Ambrosian components cannot become a Monza cathedral recension or a reception edge.

gaps.missing: Original Borromeo letters of 18 June and 16 October 1578, exact approving instrument, books affected and dated implementation; reported patriarchine rites concern mainly initiation, unction and funerals.
gaps.next_source: Original correspondence cited in Fontana, Il Duomo November 2025 pp. 22–24, and T. M. Abbiati, La Scuola cattolica 68 (1940), pp. 200–209; do not substitute the cathedral retrospective for the instrument. Lead (2026-10-21): a 2017 New Liturgical Movement photograph of the Monza cathedral museum display shows an autograph Borromeo letter to the canons labelled 1578, whose museum transcription prescribes the Roman rite in choir and sacraments and an interim Brescia or Bologna printed ritual; the handwriting is illegible at that resolution and no Mass book is named.
gaps.consequence: No dated Roman replacement, Ambrosian adoption or abolition of an independently reconstructed patriarchine Mass is plotted.
